conbody.p: Tree draws the project's hierarchy as an org chart that flows left to right: one box per artifact, with its type, ref, status and title, and elbow connectors from each parent to its children, which are stacked in the next column.

ul.li: Folding — the diagram opens with the first two levels showing. The small ⊖ on a parent's connector folds what is under it, and ⊕ (with the number of artifacts hidden beside it) unfolds it again. The fold all / unfold all button above the list does the same for every branch.

Colour by Type | Status — colours each box by its artifact type (need, requirement, design item, test case, hazard, …) or by its review status (draft, in review, approved, superseded), with a key beside the switch. The type tag and the status stay written on every box, so the colours are a second cue, never the only one.

Opening an artifact — click a box to select it and open it in the detail panel, as in the table. An artifact selected anywhere else, by a link or by ‹ / ›, unfolds the branch it sits in and comes into view.
Moving around — drag the background to pan, and use the mouse wheel or a pinch to zoom; −, + and Fit above the diagram zoom out, zoom in and fit the whole diagram on screen.

Keyboard — Tab reaches the diagram; ↑ and ↓ move between the boxes in reading order, → unfolds a box or goes to its first child, ← folds it or goes to its parent, Home and End go to the first and the last, and Enter opens the artifact. A screen reader announces the diagram as a tree, with each box's level and position.

conbody.p: On a phone, Tree shows the outline instead.
